claims.text: Adding approximately 2 at.% Si to a phosphorus-containing high-entropy or compositionally complex alloy will improve its glass-forming ability.
Adding approximately 2 at.% Si will enhance the thermal stability of the alloy's amorphous state.
The proposed intervention is alloying with approximately 2 at.% Si.
The beneficial effect requires Si to be uniformly distributed in the alloy matrix.
Controlled rapid quenching in an inert atmosphere can produce the amorphous structure required for the intervention.
The benefit occurs only within a narrow Si-concentration range near 2 at.%.
Higher Si concentrations may promote phase separation.
Higher Si concentrations may form undesired intermetallic compounds.
Si addition may enhance short-range order through the formation of Si-P clusters.
Si addition may improve local atomic packing.
The proposed short-range order or improved packing limits atomic mobility.
Reduced atomic mobility impedes the growth of crystalline nuclei.
Si addition increases local structural heterogeneity and packing efficiency by modifying interatomic interactions.
The structural changes caused by Si increase the enthalpic barrier to crystallization.
The structural changes caused by Si reduce the free volume available for nucleation.
The Si-doped alloy will have a higher DSC crystallization-onset temperature than the otherwise comparable undoped alloy.
The Si-doped alloy will require a lower critical cooling rate for glass formation than the otherwise comparable undoped alloy.
Phase separation or unwanted intermetallic formation can negate the improvement in glass-forming ability and amorphous-state thermal stability.
